question.worked_solution:
The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $x=a$ is

$$
L(x)=f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

In our case, we have $a=1,$ which gives

$$
L(x)=f(1)+{f}^{′}(1)(x-1).
$$

Let's compute $f(1)$ and ${f}^{′}(1)$ in the expression above. Evaluating the function, we get

$$
f(1)=\sqrt{1}=1,
$$

and computing the derivative, we get

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x})=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}},
$$

which in turn gives

$$
{f}^{′}(1)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1}}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is

$$
L(x)=1+\frac{1}{2}(x-1).
$$

We can approximate $\sqrt{2}$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=2.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & ≈L(2) \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2}(2-1) \\  & =1+\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
